full_judgment:
Md. Awlad Ali, J:- This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why subsection (2) of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act 8 of 2003) published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 10.3.03 making provision for depositing 25% of the decretal amount should not be declared void and as to why the impugned order dated 31.5.03 passed in Misc. Case No. 14 of 2003 of the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. The petitioner has impugned the aforesaid law impleading Bangladesh and 14 others as respondent. Concisely the facts are that the petitioner in execution proceeding being Title Execution Case No. 18/2000 initiated by the respondent no. 4 Janata Bank filed an application under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Misc. Case No. 14 of 2003 for releasing his property from attachment in that execution case. The writ petitioner claimed that he purchased 0.0167 acre of land by registered deed of sale dated 4.12.01 and he entered into possession of the purchased land. The petitioner being in possession of the said land erected semi pucca shops thereon and got electricity connection and that he inducted monthly tenants mutated his name in the revenue record and that he has been paying land revenue and taxes to the Government. The petitioner came to know from daily newspaper that the said 0.0167 acre of land was attached for auction sale in Title Execution Case No. 18 of 2000 of the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka. After making search by his appointed Advocate the petitioner came to know that the respondent no. 8 Md. Shahidullah took loan from the respondent bank by giving mortgage of 0.0935 acre of land as the said respondent failed to pay the bank loan the bank filed title suit for realisation of the outstanding dues and got a decree and put the decree in execution. The decree holder bank and the judgment debtor in collusion with each other included the property of the petitioner by showing false boundary in the proclamation of sale. In such circumstances the petitioner filed the miscellaneous case under Order 21 Rule 58 for releasing the property from attachment order which has already been sold in auction. The Artha Rin Adalat fixed the case on 13.5.03 for hearing on maintainability and after hearing rejected the miscellaneous case on 31.5.03 on the finding that as per sub-section (2) of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 the petitioner has not deposited 25% of the decretal amount. That order is also impugned in this writ petition. 

 3. The respondent no. 4 Janata Bank has filed affidavit-in-opposition. The respondent no. 14 auction purchaser has also filed affidavit-in-opposition. The respondent bank filed supplementary affidavit-in-opposition annexing some orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in the execution proceeding and it appears from Order No. 54 dated 24.2.03 that the property in question has been auction sold to the highest bidder at a value of Tk. 45,50,000/- and that being the highest price has been accepted by the Court and by that order auction purchaser was directed to deposit 1/4th of the bid money. On an application by the auction purchaer praying for time to deposit the poundage fee the case was fixed on 3.3.03. The writ petitioner filed an application under Order 21 Rule 58 on 22.5.03 when the property was sold to the respondent no.14 Shikder Creation Ltd. Order 21 Rule 58 reads as follows: 

 4. In view of the aforesaid provision one can (being a third party) make an application when the property has been attached or still under attachment in execution proceeding and the right to apply under Order 21 Rule 58 will cease to exist when the property in question has been sold in auction because if the property is sold there cannot be any order of attachment made by the Court. In the case before us the property was sold in execution proceeding on 24.2.03 and the auction purchaser paid the bid money on 5.3.03 and the petitioner made this application under the aforesaid provision on 22.5.03. Therefore, the application under Order 21 Rule 58 is apparently incompetent as the petitioner had no right to apply to the Court to make airy application for his claim after the property was sold in execution case. So the claim was not made genuinely by competent petition and the Artha Rin Adalat cannot entertain such application and that was rejected by the impugned order although on some other grounds. Since the petitioner's application was incompetent it should be rejected and that was rejected by the impugned order dated 31.5.03 and the petitioner cannot challenge the vires of section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 before this Court, for, he cannot be said to be an aggrieved person as envisaged under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

 5. Mr. Khalilur Rahman although initially put forward his argument pointing out Article 27 and 31 of the Constitution but ultimately he conceded to the proposition that after the property was sold in auction the application under Order 21 Rule 58 C.P. Code cannot be maintained. He further having seen the date of sale, the date of application under Order 21 Rule 58 C.P. Code candidly admitted that the application was not maintainable by the Adalat. Therefore, we are not called upon to decide the question of vires of section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat in this case.
